title: Novartis confirms 9 reported cases of tumors in patients treated with Zolgensma
snippet: Advocates are sounding the alarm on social media as they learn from their doctors that Novartis has received reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy.

title: RevMed’s Rasonque shatters analyst estimates with $198M quarter
snippet: Pent-up demand for the new pancreatic cancer therapy Rasonque helped RevMed soar past analysts’ sales expectations and reach 5,000 patients in the third quarter.

title: T-time: British biotech pours $133M into the pot for bispecifics
snippet: With backing from three Big Pharma investment arms, British biotech T-Therapeutics is brewing up a clinical launch for its cancer and autoimmune T cell engagers.

title: Novartis subsidiary Avidity will lay off 40 in San Diego
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Evommune inks molecular glue deal worth $1.1B biobucks to fill pipeline gap
snippet: Evommune is commiting $30 million upfront for Hinova Pharmaceuticals’ oral molecular glue degrader—a low-cost bet with a high probability of success, according to analysts, after clinical failures roiled the biotech’s internal pipeline earlier this year.

title: Coveted metabolic gem Rhythm reportedly gets $10B offer from AstraZeneca
snippet: AstraZeneca has apparently made a $10 billion bid to acquire Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, an offer William Blair suspects will not be the last for the hot ticket metabolic biotech.

title: Beyond the needle: The future of intratumoral therapy
snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from from Lewis Bender, CEO at Intensity Therapeutics and Paul-Peter Tak, president, CEO and board director at Candel Therapeutics. We explore how intratumoral therapies trigger systemic anticancer immunity from a local injection, and redefine a foundational platform in immuno...

title: The top 12 companies hiring in biopharma now
snippet: Average jobs live on BioSpace increased year over year in October, a good sign for those eyeing a new position. If that’s you, check out the list of which companies are most actively looking to hire.

title: A treatment revolution is underway in MASH
snippet: To build on the momentum in MASH, we—at Madrigal Pharmaceuticals and the industry more widely—must further expand approaches to diagnosis, monitoring and individualized treatment to help more patients.

title: 1 in 5 have had multiple biopharma layoffs, poll finds
snippet: Biotech and pharma professionals share job hunt challenges after being let go, while a recruiting expert discusses why hiring managers prefer candidates without employment gaps and how to address gaps in interviews.

title: Boehringer bets big on China, offering $7B biobucks for Sino cancer programs
snippet: Boehringer Ingelheim is building up its China strategy, inking a deal to develop new cancer treatments with Sino Biopharmaceutical just weeks after opening an R&D facility in Shanghai.

title: AbbVie bets up to $1.47B for Nxera’s discarded IBD program
snippet: AbbVie’s $100 million upfront cash payment will purchase global rights to Nxera’s deprioritized oral small molecule, which has already completed Phase 1 testing.

title: Amgen starts MariTide autoinjector study as pivotal readouts approach
snippet: With the first Phase 3 data expected for Amgen’s MariTide next year, analysts are looking for evidence that the GLP-1 candidate is tolerable. Meanwhile, the company has begun testing an autoinjector formulation.

title: Sanofi’s axing of Nurix STAT6 program ‘not a target-related issue’
snippet: Sanofi has discontinued an early-stage STAT6 degrader program licensed from Nurix Therapeutics, a decision analysts say is related to the asset itself or Sanofi’s strategic reprioritization rather than the drug class more broadly.

title: With MFN now embedded in pharma, execs see little impact from Democrats’ blue wave
snippet: Speaking on third quarter earnings calls this week, Novo and Pfizer’s CEOs see little change to their Most Favored Nation drug pricing deals, which were signed with the Trump administration last year.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Novo, Lilly battle for oral GLP-1 dominance with data tit for tat
snippet: Novo CEO Mike Maziar Doustdar insists that his company is ahead of fierce rival Eli Lilly as oral Wegovy rises to 8 million total prescriptions since its January launch.

title: Pfizer eyes Europe first for Lyme vaccine as prevalence rises in US
snippet: Since Pfizer already owns a tick-borne encephalitis franchise in Europe, the region is a natural first step for the pharma’s upcoming Lyme disease vaccine.

title: Q3 earnings roll on, FDA pushes rare disease, uniQure’s Huntington’s therapy reaches review
snippet: The majority of the large pharmas have now reported third quarter earnings—spoiler alert: Eli Lilly made more money than anyone expected. Plus, the FDA dropped another initiative aimed at accelerating rare disease treatments; HHS greenlights the compounding of six unapproved peptides; and uniQure’s embattled gene ther...

title: How a Ms. Frizzle-esque librarian helped Flagship’s Louisa Helms find biotech
snippet: BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree Louisa Helms is a lot of things—athlete, scientist, entrepreneur and likely future biotech executive. Just don’t ask her to pick up any pipettes.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
